skill.name: sast-horusec
skill.description: Guide Horusec static application security testing across local repositories and CI/CD pipelines. Supports multi-language vulnerability scanning, secrets review, severity triage, and secure SDLC reporting.
skill.summary: Run Horusec SAST, secrets checks, and CI security reporting across multi-language repositories.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from examples, reference links, or Markdown formatting. Confirmed risks include Docker socket exposure, world-writable Docker socket guidance, and remote installer scripts piped to shell. Additional supply-chain hardening is needed for mutable CI actions, scanner images, and unpinned tool installs.

remediation.issue: Docker socket exposure in scanner examples
remediation.suggestion: Remove Docker socket mounts from published examples. Use rootless Docker, isolated runners, or Horusec modes that do not bind the host socket.
Delete the chmod 666 recommendation. Use least-privilege Docker group membership or dedicated ephemeral runners instead.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts piped directly to bash
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with pinned release downloads, checksum verification, or trusted package manager instructions.

remediation.issue: Mutable CI actions, images, and package installs
remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, pin container image digests, and install exact package versions for scanner dependencies.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned CI Actions and Scanner Images
semantic_findings.description: The CI and usage guidance references mutable action refs and latest scanner images. A mutable security tool chain can change without review and expose users to compromised or inconsistent scans.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines use mutable refs and latest tags in CI or scanner execution guidance. This is a clear supply-chain hardening gap for a security scanning workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Security Tool Installation in CI Template

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template calls package installers without explicit versions. This is common in examples, but security CI templates should be reproducible and pinned.

content.user_title: Run Horusec SAST Across CI and Local Repos
content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent static analysis across languages and pipelines. This skill guides Horusec scans, secrets checks, CI setup, and finding triage.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to run Horusec scans locally and in CI.
Shows JSON output and severity threshold options.
Guides git history secret scanning and credential rotation.
Provides templates for CI security scanning and rule documentation.
Maps findings to OWASP, CWE, and MITRE ATT&CK context.
limitations: Requires Horusec CLI, Docker, or equivalent tools to execute scans.
Does not replace manual review of high-impact findings.
Generated CI examples need pinning and hardening before production use.
Scan accuracy depends on project languages, rules, and tool versions.

use_cases.title: Check code before merging
use_cases.description: Run a local Horusec scan, review critical findings, and confirm fixes before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize SAST reporting
use_cases.description: Create consistent scan outputs, severity thresholds, and remediation notes for security review workflows.

use_cases.title: Add CI security gates
use_cases.description: Use pipeline templates to run SAST, dependency, secrets, container, and IaC checks during delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Horusec scan for my current repository. Include setup checks, the scan command, and how to read high severity results.

prompt_templates.title: Review secrets exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through using Horusec to check this repository for exposed secrets. Include steps for validation, rotation, and documenting remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Design CI scanning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CI plan that runs Horusec with JSON output, stores artifacts, and fails the build on critical findings. Include hardening recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Triage complex findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me triage Horusec findings across a monorepo. Group results by severity, map them to CWE or OWASP, and propose remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: Scan a Python API repository for SAST and secrets.
output: A scan plan with prerequisites, Horusec options, and expected report files.
A triage summary grouped by critical, high, medium, and low findings.
A remediation checklist for secrets rotation and vulnerable code changes.

output_examples.input: Add Horusec to a pull request workflow.
output: A CI workflow outline with artifact retention and severity thresholds.
Notes on pinning actions, avoiding unsafe installer patterns, and limiting token permissions.
Developer feedback guidance for pull request comments and audit records.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a reported SQL injection finding is valid.
output: A finding review that checks data flow, query construction, and existing controls.
A recommended fix using parameterized queries or ORM methods.
A validation step to re-run the scan and document the result.

best_practices: Pin scanner images, actions, and installer checksums before using examples in production.
Store scan reports as restricted artifacts because they can contain sensitive code context.
Review accepted false positives on a schedule and document the business reason.
anti_patterns: Do not mount the host Docker socket into scanner containers on shared runners.
Do not pipe remote install scripts directly into a shell.
Do not treat scanner output as proof of security without human review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and operate Horusec SAST scans, secrets checks, CI integration, and security finding triage.

faq.question: Does the skill run Horusec automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands, workflows, and review guidance. You run the scanner in your own environment.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: Typical use requires Horusec, Git, and either Docker or local language security tools.

faq.question: Can it find secrets in git history?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes Horusec git history analysis and follow-up steps for credential rotation.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy the CI templates directly?
faq.answer: No. Pin actions, versions, and checksums before production use, and remove unsafe Docker socket patterns.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Validate each finding, document risk acceptance, add scoped ignore rules, and revisit accepted findings regularly.
